newsitem.title: UK: UK wheat under pressure following rate increase.
newsitem.headline: UK wheat under pressure following rate increase.

text.p: UK grain futures came under increased pressure following the announcement by the Bank of England on Wednesday that it had rised its minimum leading rate by a quarter-point to six percent.
The resulting surge by sterling against other European currencies knocked as much as 1.90 stg a tonne off wheat futures during the afternoon session.
By the close of business wheat futures were 1.10 to 1.90 stg down on a turnover of 757 lots.
Barley was unchanged in a tradeless market.
On the UK cash market fob values were around one stg a tonne down after Nov traded at 101 stg and Dec at 101.50 stg a tonne ex-east coast ports.
Delivered traded was again slow with feed wheat in East Anglia fetching from 102 down to 101 stg for Nov while in the Avon area 100.50 and 100 was paid for the same position.
November milling wheat 11 percent protein in the Liverpool area was fetching 124 stg while 120 stg was paid in the Southampton, Tewkesbury, Avonmouth and Gloucester range.
